what: A stop-motion loop that swaps stacked frame children one at a time with no in-between values — 2 frames per second (every .5s), and after the last frame it returns to the first. It replays a 9-frame animated GIF of six hands passing cards around a table using our own drawn frames. It runs only while visible and when the tab is in front.

options.fps: Frames per second, default 2 — original GIF frame length 500ms
options.hold: Section number to hold at in initial/reduced setting (from 0), default 0
options.[data-fx-part=frame]: Frames to swap (stacked — the part stands them up with absolute inset 0). The visible one gets is-on
options.fx:frame: Event fired from the element on each Section change (detail.index)
options.durs: Length per section (ms list, comma-separated) — for when lengths differ per section like the original GIF. ‹2000,500› = 2s straight → .5s tilt and nod (brand note), ”200,200” = Two photos of people walking. If given, used instead of fps
options.delay: When using durs, extra time (seconds) the first section stays longer, default 0 — offsets so several notes do not nod at the same tempo

note: The original is a GIF, so it keeps playing even when the tab is in the background, but this part stops when not visible (battery). Frame count and order are set by the markup that uses it

from.where: index.html .kk-hands (six halftone hands on the table in the Hero — original 2400px GIF, 9 frames, 2fps, 4.5s loop, rebuilt as 9 SVG frames)

svg.tp-person · svg.tp-note in index.html · about.html (people.js draws both frames) — original animated GIFs: the walking person is two frames at 200ms each (center1.gif 11 frames 200ms), the player 500ms·2000ms, the note holds 2000ms → bobs at 500ms (onpu*.gif 2000/0/500)
